title: Constrained Local Refinement of 24-Layer Dichroic
scientific_hypothesis: Limiting individual layer thickness to 150 nm and reducing optimization step size will maintain high target scores while improving robustness against manufacturing thickness errors.
design_principle: Recalled knowledge suggests that extremely thick layers in dielectric stacks can increase sensitivity to deposition rate fluctuations and internal stress; constraining thickness may force the optimizer to find more distributed phase corrections.
proposed_topology: 24-layer alternating stack on fused silica substrate, starting with tio2, ending with sio2, terminated by air.
soft_objectives: minimize deviation from 150 nm thickness cap
theory_basis: Recalled knowledge: Dichroic filters often use quarter-wave stacks modified for band edge placement.
Recalled knowledge: Thickness constraints reduce deposition error sensitivity.
Recalled knowledge: Local refinement from a high-performing seed converges faster than global search.
expected_advantages: Faster convergence due to localized search
known_risks: Uncertainty if 150 nm cap limits achievable spectral performance compared to unconstrained design.
Uncertainty about exact dispersion data for tio2/sio2 in registry.
Uncertainty about polarization splitting at 45 degrees affecting unpolarized target score.
execution_request_english: Optimize a 24-layer planar stack on fused silica using TiO2 (Siefke) and SiO2 (Gao). Incident angle 45 degrees. Wavelength bands 450-650 nm (high reflectance) and 700-1000 nm (high transmittance). Initialize thicknesses based on prior best candidate: [51.0, 57.0, 99.0, 102.0, 68.0, 78.0, 74.0, 113.0, 71.0, 73.0, 83.0, 96.0, 57.0, 58.0, 173.0, 55.0, 54.0, 57.0, 181.0, 58.0, 62.0, 74.0, 55.0, 64.0]. Constrain each layer thickness <= 150 nm during optimization. Optimizer perturbation scale 0.5 nm. Material order: alternating TiO2 (Siefke) and SiO2 (Gao) starting with TiO2 (Siefke) on substrate.
revision_reason: Feedback directive: constrain thickness and reduce step size to improve robustness.
